chunks: 37 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Ja'fi, Abu al-Hasan, narrated, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated from his father and Wahb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"While the people are standing at Arafat, a rider on a quick she-camel will come to inform them of the death of a caliph; at whose death will come the deliverance of the Family of Muhammad and the deliverance of all the people." He also said: "When you see a sign in the sky; a great fire burning for some nights in the east, then at that time will come the deliverance of the people, and it will occur a little before the appearance of al-Qa'im (peace be upon him)."

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: The One Who Rises (al-Qa'im), a title for the Mahdi
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain near Mecca where pilgrims stand during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the signs preceding the appearance of al-Qa'im according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the transition from the era of the Caliphs to the era of the Imam, framing the caliph's death as a precursor to the 'Furaj' (deliverance) of the Ahl al-Bayt. The celestial fire in the east serves as a cosmic confirmation of the imminent appearance of al-Qa'im, a sign often linked in Shia eschatology to the 'Sign of the Rising' mentioned in prophetic traditions. These events underscore the divine timing of the Mahdi's emergence, marking the end of political concealment and the beginning of global justice.
